facts.text: Newcastle was founded in 1910 by residents relocating from the more isolated community of Pinto in search of better agricultural opportunities.
The name Newcastle was inspired by the castellated appearance of the surrounding cliffs, with the word new added to signify a fresh start.
Newcastle is a small farming community that produces wheat, oats, alfalfa, corn, and potatoes, along with dairy and greenhouse plants.
Newcastle lies within the Escalante Desert, a high-desert basin located between the Basin and Range Province and the Colorado Plateau.
Prominent mountain ranges encircling Newcastle rise to over 8,000 feet, creating localized variations in temperature and precipitation.
The local economy of Newcastle centers on agriculture, forestry, fishing, and hunting, supplemented by transportation and educational services.
